The final result turns that scalar profile into an identifiability theorem: arbitrarily local data near the geometrically distinguished Hilbert exponent recover every component Euclidean distortion and multiplicity. The cusp coefficient provides an immediately readable structural diagnostic of tied worst summands, while a unique worst summand is infinitely flat. This is a natural inverse question attached to the source theorem, not an arbitrary parameter slice or a recomputation of a known table.
